# Ear Guards

> Practical guides and comparisons for choosing ear protection for work, sleep, shooting, concerts, and everyday noise.

Ear Guards (EarGuards.com) publishes free buying guides and plain-English hearing-safety explainers. Some product links are Amazon Associates links (tag earguards-20). Range and hunting guidance is in the shooting guide. Concert and musician plugs are in the concerts guide. Travel plugs are in the sleeping guide. The site does not publish a separate flying guide.

## Start here

- [Home](https://earguards.com/): Overview of guides, use-case categories, and a short noise-level preview.
- [Best ear protection](https://earguards.com/best-ear-protection): Buying guides organized by use case, including work, shooting, sleep, concerts, kids, motorsports, and sensory needs.
- [Hearing safety guides](https://earguards.com/hearing-safety-guides): Explainers on noise reduction ratings, safe decibel limits, and ear plugs versus ear muffs.
- [Blog](https://earguards.com/blog): Index of every guide on the site.

## Tools

- [Printable range NRR card](https://earguards.com/range-nrr-card): Free one-page card on what a package Noise Reduction Rating means at a firing line. No products or prices.
- [Range NRR card PDF](https://earguards.com/range-nrr-card.pdf): The same card as a downloadable US Letter PDF.
- [Noise level database](https://earguards.com/noise-level-database): Decibel chart of everyday sounds and which levels call for hearing protection.
- [OSHA hearing protection](https://earguards.com/osha-hearing-protection): Plain-English overview of OSHA hearing-conservation rules, including the 85 dBA action level and the 90 dBA exposure limit.

## Guides

- [Best ear protection for shooting](https://earguards.com/blog/best-ear-protection-for-shooting): Electronic and passive options for ranges and hunting, and when to wear plugs under muffs indoors.
- [Best ear protection for concerts](https://earguards.com/blog/best-ear-protection-for-concerts): High-fidelity plugs that lower concert volume without muffling the music, including options for musicians.
- [Best ear protection for construction workers](https://earguards.com/blog/best-ear-protection-for-construction-workers): Job-site plugs and muffs, with NRR guidance by role and notes on all-day comfort.
- [Best ear plugs for sleeping](https://earguards.com/blog/best-ear-plugs-for-sleeping): Foam, silicone, and reusable plugs for snoring, traffic, and side sleeping. Also the travel pick.
- [Best ear protection for kids](https://earguards.com/blog/best-ear-protection-for-kids): Age-sized earmuffs for babies, toddlers, and children at fireworks, events, and travel.
- [Best ear protection for motorcycle riders](https://earguards.com/blog/best-ear-protection-for-motorcycle-riders): Low-profile plugs for wind noise inside a helmet, including options that keep traffic audible.
- [Best ear protection for sensory sensitivity](https://earguards.com/blog/best-ear-protection-for-sensory-sensitivity): Comfort-first muffs and plugs for autism, ADHD, and sensory processing differences.
- [Ear plugs vs ear muffs](https://earguards.com/blog/ear-plugs-vs-ear-muffs): NRR, comfort, and cost compared, with which to choose for work, sleep, and shooting.
- [What is noise reduction rating?](https://earguards.com/blog/what-is-noise-reduction-rating): What the package NRR means, and a common way to estimate real-world protection.
- [How many decibels can damage hearing?](https://earguards.com/blog/how-many-decibels-can-damage-hearing): Loudness thresholds and how exposure time changes the risk.
